extraction_notes.note: The protocols P, Q' and the correlated-sampling protocol are framed (mdframed) procedures inside proofs; the step gloss says a construction inside a proof stays proof_steps, but these are named, cited protocols, so each is an algorithm node nested in the proof step that introduces it.

Uncited \begin{fact} environments mapped to claim per Hard rule 4; those proved in the paper (2.6, 2.10, 2.12) are origin paper, the three whose proofs are skipped as 'direct calculations' (2.13-2.15) are external standard results.

The introduction's informal statements of P and P' (fidelity 1-eps, success probability 1-4eps) differ from Theorems 3.1/3.12 (fidelity 1-5eps); only the theorem copies were kept. Fact 2.8 is titled 'Quantum substrate theorem' (a typo for substate); the canonical name is used.

Abstract/introduction restatements of P, P', P_1, the intro sketch of the quantum protocol, minor notation (cross products, sub-normalized states, isometries, U(A)), Touchette's results mentioned in passing and the vague third open question were not made nodes.
The proof of Claim 3.7 is written in prose (\noindent{\em Proof of Claim...}) after the proof of Claim 3.9, inside the proof of Theorem 3.1; taken as a prose proof node nested in a setup step.

nodes.name: Direct sum result
nodes.statement: A direct sum result for a relation $f$ in a model of communication  (roughly) states that in order to compute $k$ independent  instances of $f$ simultaneously, if we provide communication less than $k$ times the communication required to compute $f$ with the constant success probability $p<1$, then the success probability for computing all the $k$ instances of $f$ correctly is at most a constant $q<1$.
nodes.statement_short: A direct sum result: computing k independent instances with less than k times the single-instance communication succeeds with probability at most a constant q<1.

nodes.name: Direct product result
nodes.statement: A direct product result, which is a stronger result, states that in such a situation  the success probability for computing all the $k$ instances of $f$ correctly is at most $p^{-\Omega(k)}$.
nodes.statement_short: A direct product result: under the same conditions the success probability on all k instances is exponentially small in k.

nodes.name: Braverman-Rao sampling protocol
nodes.statement: In the protocol of~\cite{Braverman2011}, Alice and Bob share (as public coins) $\{(M_i,R_i)|~ i \in \mathbb{N}\}$, where each $(M_i,R_i)$ is independently and identically distributed uniformly over $\CMcal{U}\times[0,1]$, $\CMcal{U}$ being the support of $P$ and $Q$. Alice accepts index $i$ iff $ R_i \leq P(M_i) $ and Bob accepts index $i$ iff $ R_i \leq  2^c Q(M_i) $.
input: inputs to Alice and Bob are classical probability distributions $P,Q$ respectively
nodes.statement_short: Classical rejection-sampling protocol with shared public coins: Alice and Bob accept indices of shared uniform samples under P and 2^c Q respectively.

nodes.name: Share public coins
nodes.statement: Alice and Bob share (as public coins) $\{(M_i,R_i)|~ i \in \mathbb{N}\}$, where each $(M_i,R_i)$ is independently and identically distributed uniformly over $\CMcal{U}\times[0,1]$, $\CMcal{U}$ being the support of $P$ and $Q$.
nodes.statement_short: Share i.i.d. uniform pairs (M_i,R_i) over U x [0,1].

nodes.name: Acceptance tests
nodes.statement: Alice accepts index $i$ iff $ R_i \leq P(M_i) $ and Bob accepts index $i$ iff $ R_i \leq  2^c Q(M_i) $.
nodes.statement_short: Alice accepts i iff R_i <= P(M_i); Bob iff R_i <= 2^c Q(M_i).

nodes.name: Braverman-Rao index communication
nodes.statement: Braverman and Rao argue that Alice can communicate this index $j$ to Bob, with high probability, using communication of $\CMcal{O}(c)$ bits (for constant ${\varepsilon}$), using crucially the fact that $P \leq 2^c Q $.
conclusions: Alice can communicate this index $j$ to Bob, with high probability, using communication of $\CMcal{O}(c)$ bits (for constant ${\varepsilon}$)
nodes.statement_short: In the classical protocol, Alice can send her first accepted index to Bob with O(c) bits w.h.p.

nodes.name: Task T1
nodes.statement: \noindent {\bf T1}:  Alice gets to know the eigen-decomposition of a quantum state $\rho$. Alice and Bob get to know the eigen-decomposition of a quantum state $\sigma$, such that $\text{supp}(\rho) \subset \text{supp}(\sigma)$. They also know $c \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \relent{\rho}{\sigma}$, the relative entropy between $\rho$ and $\sigma$ and an error parameter ${\varepsilon}$. They  use shared entanglement and communication and at the end of the protocol, Bob ends up with a quantum state $\tilde{\rho}$ such that $\mathrm{F}(\rho, \tilde{\rho}) \geq 1 - {\varepsilon}$.
nodes.statement_short: Transmit a state rho to Bob with fidelity 1-eps, where both know sigma and S(rho||sigma), using entanglement and communication.

nodes.name: Jain-Radhakrishnan-Sen compression
nodes.statement: Jain, Radhakrishnan and Sen in~\cite{Jain:2005:PEM:1068502.1068658,Jain:2008}, showed that this task  (for constant ${\varepsilon}$) can be achieved with  communication $\CMcal{O}(\relent{\rho}{\sigma} +1)$ bits, and this led to direct sum theorems for all relations in  entanglement-assisted quantum one-way and entanglement-assisted quantum simultaneous message-passing communication models.
conclusions: this task  (for constant ${\varepsilon}$) can be achieved with  communication $\CMcal{O}(\relent{\rho}{\sigma} +1)$ bits
nodes.statement_short: Task T1 can be achieved with O(S(rho||sigma)+1) bits of communication.

nodes.name: Jain-Radhakrishnan-Sen classical compression
nodes.statement: They also considered the special case when the inputs to Alice and Bob are probability distributions $P,Q$ respectively and showed that sharing public random coins and $\CMcal{O}(\relent{P}{Q}+1))$ bits of  communication can achieve this task (for constant ${\varepsilon}$).
assumptions: the inputs to Alice and Bob are probability distributions $P,Q$ respectively
conclusions: sharing public random coins and $\CMcal{O}(\relent{P}{Q}+1))$ bits of  communication can achieve this task (for constant ${\varepsilon}$)

nodes.name: Harsha-Jain-McAllester-Radhakrishnan sampling
nodes.statement: Later an improved result was obtained by Harsha, Jain, Mc. Allester and Radhakrishnan~\cite{Harsha:2010}, where they presented a protocol in which Bob is able to sample exactly from $P$ with expected communication $\relent{P}{Q}+2\log\relent{P}{Q}+\CMcal{O}(1)$.
conclusions: Bob is able to sample exactly from $P$ with expected communication $\relent{P}{Q}+2\log\relent{P}{Q}+\CMcal{O}(1)$
nodes.statement_short: Bob can sample exactly from P with expected communication S(P||Q)+2 log S(P||Q)+O(1).

nodes.name: [n]
nodes.statement: For integer $n \geq 1$, let $[n]$ represent the set $\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$.

nodes.name: Logarithm notation
nodes.statement: We let $\log$ represent logarithm to the base $2$ and $\ln$ represent logarithm to the base $\mathrm{e}$.

nodes.name: Expectation
nodes.statement_short: Expectation of f under distribution X is the probability-weighted sum.

nodes.name: l1 and l2 norms
nodes.statement: The $\ell_1$ norm of an operator $X$ on $\CMcal{H}$ is $\onenorm{X}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }\sqrt{X^{\dag}X}$ and $\ell_2$ norm is $\norm{X}_2\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\sqrt{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } XX^{\dag}}$.

nodes.name: Quantum state
nodes.statement: A quantum state (or a density matrix or just a state) is a positive semi-definite matrix with trace equal to $1$.

nodes.name: Pure state
nodes.statement: It is called {\em pure} if and only if the rank is $1$.

nodes.name: Pure-state notation
nodes.statement: With some abuse of notation, we use $\psi$ to represent the state and also the density matrix $\ketbra{\psi}$, associated with $\ket{\psi}$.

nodes.name: Computational basis
nodes.statement: Fix an orthonormal basis on $\CMcal{H}$, referred to as {\em computational basis}.

nodes.name: Complex conjugation
nodes.statement: Let $\conjugate{\ket{\psi}}$ represent the complex conjugation of $\ket{\psi}$, taken in the computational basis.

nodes.name: Support
nodes.statement: Given a quantum state $\rho$ on $\CMcal{H}$, {\em support of $\rho$}, called $\text{supp}(\rho)$ is the subspace of $\CMcal{H}$ spanned by all eigen-vectors of $\rho$ with non-zero eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Quantum register
nodes.statement: A {\em quantum register} $A$ is associated with some Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}_A$.

nodes.name: |A|
nodes.statement: Define $|A| \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \dim(\CMcal{H}_A)$.

nodes.name: L(A)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{L}(A)$ represent the set of all linear operators on $\CMcal{H}_A$.

nodes.name: D(A)
nodes.statement: We denote by $\mathcal{D}(A)$, the set of quantum states on the Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}_A$.

nodes.name: Register equivalence
nodes.statement: If two registers $A,B$ are associated with the same Hilbert space, we shall represent the relation by $A\equiv B$.

nodes.name: Register composition
nodes.statement: Composition of two registers $A$ and $B$, denoted $AB$, is associated with Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}_A \otimes \CMcal{H}_B$.

nodes.name: Identity operator
nodes.statement: The identity operator on $\CMcal{H}_A$ (and associated register $A$) is denoted $I_A$.

nodes.name: Partial trace
nodes.statement:
Let $\rho_{AB} \in \mathcal{D}(AB)$. We define
\[ \rho_{\reg{B}} \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \partrace{\reg{A}}{\rho_{AB}}
\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \sum_i (\bra{i} \otimes I_{\cspace{B}})
\rho_{AB} (\ket{i} \otimes I_{\cspace{B}}) , \]
where $\set{\ket{i}}_i$ is an orthonormal basis for the Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}_A$.
nodes.statement_short: Partial trace over A: rho_B = sum_i (<i| x I) rho_AB (|i> x I).

nodes.name: Marginal state
nodes.statement: The state $\rho_B\in \mathcal{D}(B)$ is referred to as the marginal state of $\rho_{AB}$.

nodes.name: Purification
nodes.statement: Given a $\rho_A\in\mathcal{D}(A)$, a {\em purification} of $\rho_A$ is a pure state $\rho_{AB}\in \mathcal{D}(AB)$ such that $\partrace{\reg{B}}{\rho_{AB}}=\rho_A$.

nodes.name: Quantum map
nodes.statement: A quantum {map} $\mathcal{E}: \mathcal{L}(A)\rightarrow \mathcal{L}(B)$ is a completely positive and trace preserving (CPTP) linear map (mapping states in $\mathcal{D}(A)$ to states in $\mathcal{D}(B)$).

nodes.name: Unitary operator
nodes.statement: A {\em unitary} operator $U_A:\CMcal{H}_A \rightarrow \CMcal{H}_A$ is such that $U_A^{\dagger}U_A = U_A U_A^{\dagger} = I_A$.

nodes.name: Information theoretic quantities
nodes.statement:
We shall consider the following information theoretic quantities. Let $A$ be a quantum register. Let $\varepsilon \geq 0$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item {\bf Fidelity} For $\rho,\sigma \in \mathcal{D}(A)$, $$\mathrm{F}(\rho,\sigma)\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\onenorm{\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma}}.$$ For classical probability distributions $P = \{p_i\}, Q =\{q_i\}$, $$\mathrm{F}(P,Q)\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \sum_i \sqrt{p_i \cdot q_i}.$$

\item {\bf Entropy} For $\rho\in\mathcal{D}(A)$, $$S(\rho_A) \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } - \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(\rho_A\log\rho_A) .$$ 
\item {\bf Relative entropy} For $\rho,\sigma\in \mathcal{D}(A)$ such that $\text{supp}(\rho) \subset \text{supp}(\sigma)$, $$\relent{\rho}{\sigma} \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(\rho\log\rho) - \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(\rho\log\sigma) .$$ 
\item {\bf Relative max-entropy} For $\rho,\sigma\in \mathcal{D}(A)$ such that $\text{supp}(\rho) \subset \text{supp}(\sigma)$, $$ \rminent{\rho}{\sigma}  \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }  \inf \{ \lambda \in \mathbb{R} : 2^{\lambda} \sigma \geq \rho \}  .$$
\item {\bf Mutual information} For $\rho_{AB}\in \mathcal{D}(AB)$, $$\mutinf{A}{B}_{\rho}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } S(\rho_A) + S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}) = \relent{\rho_{AB}}{\rho_A\otimes\rho_B}.$$
\item {\bf Conditional mutual information} For $\rho_{ABC}\in\mathcal{D}(ABC)$, $$\condmutinf{A}{B}{C}_{\rho}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \mutinf{A}{BC}_{\rho}-\mutinf{A}{C}_{\rho}.$$
\end{enumerate}
nodes.definiendum: Fidelity, entropy, relative entropy, relative max-entropy, mutual information, conditional mutual information
nodes.statement_short: Defines fidelity, von Neumann entropy, relative entropy, relative max-entropy, mutual information and conditional mutual information.
nodes.label: def:infquant

nodes.name: Fuchs-van de Graaf inequalities
nodes.statement:
For quantum states $\rho,\sigma \in \mathcal{D}(A)$, it holds that
	\[2(1-\mathrm{F}(\rho,\sigma))\leq\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}\leq2\sqrt{1-\mathrm{F}(\rho,\sigma)^2}.\]
For two pure states $\ket{\phi}$ and $\ket{\psi}$, we have
\[\onenorm{\phi-\psi}=2 \sqrt{1-\mathrm{F}(\phi, \psi)^2}=2 \sqrt{1-\abs{\langle\phi|\psi\rangle}^2}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Trace distance is sandwiched between 2(1-F) and 2 sqrt(1-F^2), with equality on the right for pure states.
nodes.label: fact:tracefidelityequi

nodes.name: Stinespring representation
nodes.statement: (\textbf{Stinespring representation}) Let $\mathcal{E}(\cdot): \mathcal{L}(A)\rightarrow \mathcal{L}(B)$ be a quantum operation. There exists a Hilbert space $C$ and an unitary $U: A \otimes B \otimes C \rightarrow A \otimes B\otimes C$ such that $\mathcal{E}(\omega)=\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }_{A,C}\br{U (\omega  \otimes \ketbra{0}^{B,C}) U^{\dagger}}$. Stinespring representation for a channel is not unique.
conclusions: There exists a Hilbert space $C$ and an unitary $U: A \otimes B \otimes C \rightarrow A \otimes B\otimes C$
nodes.label: stinespring

nodes.name: Monotonicity under quantum operations
nodes.statement_short: Trace distance and relative entropy do not increase, and fidelity does not decrease, under quantum operations (e.g. partial trace).
nodes.label: fact:monotonequantumoperation

nodes.name: Trace norm versus Hilbert-Schmidt norm of square roots
nodes.statement:
Let $A, B$ be two positive semidefinite operators on Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}$. Then
\[\onenorm{A-B}\geq\norm{\sqrt{A}-\sqrt{B}}^2_2.\]
assumptions: Let $A, B$ be two positive semidefinite operators on Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}$.
nodes.label: fact:onenorm vs twonorm

nodes.name: Trace of root product vs trace distance
nodes.statement:
Given two quantum states $\rho$ and $\sigma$, 
$$\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma}\geq 1 - \frac{1}{2} \onenorm{ \rho - \sigma} \geq 1-\sqrt{1-\mathrm{F}(\rho,\sigma)^2} .$$
nodes.label: fact:fidelityvstrace

nodes.name: Proof of Fact 2.6
nodes.statement:
By  Facts~\ref{fact:onenorm vs twonorm} and~\ref{fact:tracefidelityequi},
\[2\sqrt{1-\mathrm{F}(\rho,\sigma)^2}\geq \onenorm{ \rho - \sigma } \geq\norm{\sqrt{\rho}-\sqrt{\sigma}}_2^2=2-2 \cdot \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }\br{\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma}}. \tag*{\qedhere}\]
nodes.statement_short: Combine Fact 2.5 with the Fuchs-van de Graaf bound, expanding the Hilbert-Schmidt norm.

nodes.name: Joint concavity of fidelity
nodes.statement: [\cite{Watrouslecturenote}, Proposition 4.7] Given states $\rho_1,\rho_2\ldots\rho_k,\sigma_1,\sigma_2\ldots\sigma_k$ and positive numbers $p_1,p_2\ldots p_k$ such that $\sum_ip_i=1$. Then $$\mathrm{F}(\sum_ip_i\rho_i,\sum_ip_i\sigma_i)\geq \sum_ip_i\mathrm{F}(\rho_i,\sigma_i).$$
assumptions: Given states $\rho_1,\rho_2\ldots\rho_k,\sigma_1,\sigma_2\ldots\sigma_k$ and positive numbers $p_1,p_2\ldots p_k$ such that $\sum_ip_i=1$.
nodes.label: fact:fidconcave

nodes.name: Quantum substate theorem
nodes.statement:
(\textbf{Quantum substrate theorem}) Given $\rho, \sigma \in \mathcal{D}(A)$, such that $\text{supp}(\rho) \subset \text{supp}(\sigma)$. For any ${\varepsilon}>0$, there exists $\rho'\in \mathcal{D}(A)$ such that
\[\mathrm{F}(\rho,\rho')\geq1-{\varepsilon}\quad \mbox{and}\quad \rminent{\rho'}{\sigma}\leq\frac{\relent{\rho}{\sigma}+1}{{\varepsilon}}+\log\frac{1}{1-{\varepsilon}}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Any rho can be perturbed to rho' with fidelity 1-eps whose relative max-entropy to sigma is about (S(rho||sigma)+1)/eps.
nodes.label: fact:substrate

nodes.name: Gentle measurement lemma
nodes.statement:
(\textbf{Gentle measurement lemma}) Let $\rho\in \mathcal{D}(A)$  and $\Pi$ be a projector. Then,
\[\mathrm{F}(\rho,\frac{\Pi \rho \Pi}{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } \Pi \rho })\geq \sqrt{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } \Pi \rho}.\]
nodes.label: fact:gentlemeasurement

nodes.name: Proof of the gentle measurement lemma
nodes.statement:
Introduce a register $B$, such that $|B|\geq |A|$. Let $\phi\in \mathcal{D}(AB)$ be a purification of $\rho$. Then $( \Pi \otimes I_B)\phi ( \Pi \otimes I_B)$ is a purification of $\Pi \rho \Pi $. Hence  (using monotonicity of fidelity under quantum operation, Fact~\ref{fact:monotonequantumoperation})
\[\mathrm{F}(\rho, \frac{\Pi \rho \Pi}{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } \Pi \rho } )\mathrm{F}\br{\phi,(\Pi\otimes I_B)\phi(\Pi\otimes I_B)}= \frac{\abs{\bra{\phi}(\Pi \otimes I) \ket{\phi}}}{\norm{(\Pi \otimes I) \ket{\phi}}}  = \sqrt{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }( \Pi \rho)}.   \tag*{\qedhere} \]
nodes.statement_short: Purify rho and apply monotonicity of fidelity under partial trace to the projected purification.

nodes.name: Trace bound on exponential of log-sum
nodes.statement:
Given quantum states $\sigma_{AB}\in \mathcal{D}(AB), \rho_A\in \mathcal{D}(A)$, such that $\text{supp}(\rho_A)\subset\text{supp}(\sigma_A)$, it holds that 
$$\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(e^{\text{log}(\sigma_{AB})-\text{log}(\sigma_{A}\otimes I_B)+\text{log}(\rho_{A}\otimes I_B)})<1.$$
nodes.statement_short: Tr exp(log sigma_AB - log sigma_A + log rho_A) < 1.
nodes.label: fact:ruskai

nodes.name: Proof of Fact 2.10
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lieb-Ruskai's integral representation bound (Theorem 5 of [ruskai2002]) and integrate.

nodes.name: Strong subadditivity theorem
nodes.statement: ~\cite{Lieb:1973,LiebR:1973}(\textbf{Strong subadditivity theorem}) For any tripartite quantum state $\rho\in\mathcal{D}(ABC)$, it holds that $\condmutinf{A}{C}{B}_{\rho}\geq0$.
nodes.label: fact:strongsubadditivity

nodes.name: Araki-Lieb and subadditivity inequalities
nodes.statement:
For a quantum state $\rho_{AB}\in\mathcal{D}(AB)$, it holds that $\abs{\mathrm{S}(\rho_A)-\mathrm{S}(\rho_B)}\leq\mathrm{S}(\rho_{AB})\leq\mathrm{S}(\rho_A)+\mathrm{S}(\rho_B)$. Furthermore,
\[\mutinf{A}{B}_{\rho}=\mathrm{S}(\rho_A)+\mathrm{S}(\rho_B)-\mathrm{S}(\rho_{AB})\leq 2\mathrm{S}(\rho_A).\]
nodes.statement_short: Araki-Lieb and subadditivity bounds on joint entropy; mutual information is at most twice a marginal entropy.
nodes.label: fact:conditionalmutinf

nodes.name: Superadditivity of conditional mutual information over independent registers
nodes.statement:
Let $\rho_{A_1A_2\ldots A_kBC} \in \mathcal{D}(A_1\cdots A_k BC)$ such that $\rho_{A_1A_2\ldots A_k}=\rho_{A_1}\otimes\rho_{A_2}\otimes\ldots\rho_{A_k}$. Then,
\[\condmutinf{A_1A_2\ldots A_k}{B}{C}_{\rho}\geq\sum_{i=1}^k\condmutinf{A_i}{B}{C}_{\rho}.\]
assumptions: Let $\rho_{A_1A_2\ldots A_kBC} \in \mathcal{D}(A_1\cdots A_k BC)$ such that $\rho_{A_1A_2\ldots A_k}=\rho_{A_1}\otimes\rho_{A_2}\otimes\ldots\rho_{A_k}$.
nodes.statement_short: For independent A_1..A_k, I(A_1...A_k:B|C) is at least the sum of I(A_i:B|C).
nodes.label: fact:chainrulemutualinf

nodes.name: Proof of Fact 2.12
nodes.statement_short: By induction on k: chain rule, independence of A_1 from the rest, and strong subadditivity.

nodes.name: Relative entropy splitting for cq states
nodes.statement:
Given $\rho_{AB},\sigma_{AB}\in\mathcal{D}(AB)$, such that $\text{supp}(\sigma_{AB})\subset \text{supp}(\rho_{AB})$, $\rho_{AB} = \sum_a \mu(a) \ketbra{a}_A \otimes\rho^a_B$ and
	$\sigma_{AB} = \sum_a \mu'(a) \ketbra{a}_A \otimes\sigma^a_B$, where $\rho^a_B,\sigma^a_B\in \mathcal{D}(B)$, $\mu(a),\mu'(a)\geq 0$ and $\sum_a\mu(a)=1,\sum_a\mu'(a)=1$.
	It holds from the definition of relative entropy that
	\[ \relent{\sigma_{AB}}{\rho_{AB}} = \relent{\mu}{\mu'}
	+ \expec{a\leftarrow \mu'} {\relent{\sigma^a_B}{\rho^a_B}}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Relative entropy of classical-quantum states splits as classical part plus average conditional relative entropy.
nodes.label: fact:relative entropy splitting

nodes.name: Holevo formula for cq mutual information
nodes.statement:
Given a classical-quantum state $\rho_{AB}\in \mathcal{D}(AB)$ of the form
$\rho_{AB} = \sum_a \mu(a) \ketbra{a}_A \otimes \rho^a_B$,
where $\rho^a_B\in\mathcal{D}(B)$ and $\sum_a \mu(a)=1$, $\mu(a)\geq 0$, we have
\[ \mutinf{A}{B}_{\rho}
= \mathrm{S}\br{\sum_a\mu(a)\rho_a}-\sum_a\mu(a)\mathrm{S}\br{\rho_a},\]
nodes.statement_short: For a cq state, I(A:B) = S(average state) - average S(rho_a).

nodes.name: Conditional mutual information of cq states
nodes.statement:
Let $\rho_{ABC}$ be a state of the form $\rho_{ABC}=\sum_c \mu(c)\ketbra{c}_{C}\otimes \rho^c_{AB}$, where $\rho^c_{AB}\in\mathcal{D}(AB)$ and $\sum_c\mu(c)=1$, $\mu(c)\geq 0$. Then
$$\condmutinf{A}{B}{C}_{\rho}=\sum_c \mu(c)\mutinf{A}{B}_{\rho^c}.$$
assumptions: Let $\rho_{ABC}$ be a state of the form $\rho_{ABC}=\sum_c \mu(c)\ketbra{c}_{C}\otimes \rho^c_{AB}$, where $\rho^c_{AB}\in\mathcal{D}(AB)$ and $\sum_c\mu(c)=1$, $\mu(c)\geq 0$.
nodes.label: fact:cqcondmut

nodes.name: Entanglement assisted quantum one-way protocol
nodes.statement: Let $f\subseteq\CMcal{X}\times\CMcal{Y}\times\CMcal{Z}$ be a relation. Alice holds input $x \in \CMcal{X}$ and Bob holds input $y \in \CMcal{Y}$. They may share prior quantum states independent of the inputs. Alice makes a unitary transformation on her qubits, based on her input $x$, and sends part of her qubits to Bob. Bob makes a unitary operation, based on his input $y$, and measures the last few qubits (answer registers) in the computational basis to get the answer $z \in \CMcal{Z}$. The answer is declared correct if $(x,y,z)\in f$.
nodes.statement_short: One-way model: Alice applies an input-dependent unitary and sends qubits; Bob applies a unitary and measures the answer z, correct if (x,y,z) in f.

nodes.name: Quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement: Let $\qcc{{\varepsilon}}{f}$ represent the quantum one-way communication complexity of $f$ with worst case error ${\varepsilon}$, that is minimum number of qubits Alice needs to send to Bob, over all protocols computing $f$ with error at most ${\varepsilon}$ on \textit{any} input $(x,y)$.
nodes.statement_short: Q^{ent,A->B}_eps(f): minimum qubits Alice sends over protocols with worst-case error at most eps.

nodes.name: Distributional quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement: We let $\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}}{f}$ represent distributional quantum one-way communication complexity of $f$ under distribution $\mu$ over $\CMcal{X}\times \CMcal{Y}$ with distributional error at most ${\varepsilon}$. This is the communication cost of the best protocol computing $f$ with maximum error ${\varepsilon}$ averaged over distribution $\mu$.
nodes.statement_short: Distributional complexity: cost of the best protocol with error at most eps averaged over mu.

nodes.name: Yao's min-max theorem
nodes.statement:
\cite{Yao:1979:CQR:800135.804414}
$\qcc{{\varepsilon}}{f}=\max_{\mu}\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}}{f}$.
nodes.label: fact:yaos principle

nodes.name: Quantum compression protocol P
nodes.statement: Given quantum states $\rho,\sigma$ on a Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}$ with dimension $N$, such that $\text{supp}(\rho) \subset \text{supp}(\sigma)$. Alice is given the eigen-decomposition of $\rho$ and Bob is given the eigen-decomposition of $\sigma$. Let  $\relent{\rho}{\sigma}$ and ${\varepsilon} >0$ be known to Alice and Bob. There exists an entanglement assisted quantum one-way communication protocol, with Alice sending $\CMcal{O}(\relent{\rho}{\sigma}+1)/{\varepsilon}^4)$ bits of communication to Bob, such that the state $\tilde{\rho}$ that Bob outputs at the end of the protocol satisfies  $\mathrm{F}(\rho,\tilde{\rho})\geq 1-5{\varepsilon}$ .
assumptions: Given quantum states $\rho,\sigma$ on a Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}$ with dimension $N$, such that $\text{supp}(\rho) \subset \text{supp}(\sigma)$.
Alice is given the eigen-decomposition of $\rho$ and Bob is given the eigen-decomposition of $\sigma$.
Let  $\relent{\rho}{\sigma}$ and ${\varepsilon} >0$ be known to Alice and Bob.
conclusions: There exists an entanglement assisted quantum one-way communication protocol, with Alice sending $\CMcal{O}(\relent{\rho}{\sigma}+1)/{\varepsilon}^4)$ bits of communication to Bob, such that the state $\tilde{\rho}$ that Bob outputs at the end of the protocol satisfies  $\mathrm{F}(\rho,\tilde{\rho})\geq 1-5{\varepsilon}$ .
nodes.statement_short: With shared entanglement, Alice can transmit rho to Bob (who knows sigma) to fidelity 1-5eps using O((S(rho||sigma)+1)/eps^4) bits.
nodes.label: thm:protocol

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1 (protocol P and analysis)
nodes.statement_short: Construction: quantum rejection sampling on shared maximally entangled states plus hashing of Alice's accepted index. The key step bounds Bob's conditional acceptance via the quantum substate theorem applied to rho'.

nodes.name: Shared state |S>
nodes.statement: \ket{S}_{A_1A_2B_1B_2} \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{1}{\sqrt{KN}}\sum_{i=1}^N \ket{i,i}_{A_1B_1} \otimes \left( \sum_{m=1}^{K}\ket{m, m}_{A_2B_2} \right)
nodes.label: eq:sharedstate

nodes.name: Alice's projector P_A
nodes.statement: P_A\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\sum_i\ket{a_i}_{A_1}\bra{a_i}_{A_1}\otimes\left(\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m}_{A_2}\bra{m}_{A_2}\right) .
nodes.label: eq:aliceproj

nodes.name: Bob's projector P_B
nodes.statement: P_B\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \sum_i\ket{b_i}_{B_1}\bra{b_i}_{B_1}\otimes\left(\sum_{m=1}^{\min\{\frac{K}{\delta} 2^{c'} b_i,K\}}\ket{m}_{B_2}\bra{m}_{B_2}\right) .
nodes.label: eq:bobproj

nodes.name: Success probabilities
nodes.statement: For each index $i$, $\prob{\text{Alice succeeds}}=\frac{1}{N}$; $\prob{\text{Bob succeeds}}\leq\frac{2^{c'}}{\delta N}$
nodes.label: claim:successprob

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.2
nodes.statement: Follows from direct calculation.
nodes.statement_short: Direct calculation.

nodes.name: Overlap of rho' eigenvectors with small eigenspaces of sigma
nodes.statement: Let $\rho'$ have the eigen-decomposition $\rho' = \sum_i g_i\ket{g_i}\bra{g_i}$. For any $p>0$ and every $\ket{g_i}\bra{g_i}$, we have $\sum_{j|~b_j\leq p\cdot g_i}\abs{\braket{b_j}{g_i}}^2 \leq 2^{c'}\cdot p$.
nodes.statement_short: Eigenvectors of rho' have weight at most 2^{c'} p on sigma's eigenvectors with eigenvalue at most p g_i.
nodes.label: claim:1

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.3
nodes.statement: Since  $\rho' \leq 2^{c'}\sigma$, it implies $g_i\ket{g_i}\bra{g_i} \leq 2^{c'}\sigma$. Let $\Pi$ be the projection onto the eigen-space of $\sigma$ with eigenvalues less than or equal to $p\cdot g_i$. We have $\Pi\sigma\Pi \leq p\cdot g_i\cdot\Pi$. After applying $\Pi$ on both sides of the equation $g_i\ket{g_i}\bra{g_i} \leq 2^{c'}\sigma$ and taking operator norm on both sides, we get $g_i\sum_{j:~b_j \leq p\cdot g_i}\abs{\braket{b_j}{g_i}}^2 \leq 2^{c'}\cdot p \cdot g_i $. This implies the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Project the operator inequality g_i|g_i><g_i| <= 2^{c'} sigma onto sigma's small-eigenvalue subspace and take norms.

nodes.name: Closeness of S_A(rho) and S_A(rho')
nodes.statement: $\abs{\braket{S_A(\rho)}{S_A(\rho')}} \geq 1- 2 (1-\mathrm{F}(\rho,\rho'))^{1/4} .$
nodes.label: claim:2

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.4
nodes.statement_short: Express the overlap as sum of minima of two distributions R, R' and bound via trace distance and fidelity relations.

nodes.name: Bob succeeds given Alice succeeds
nodes.statement: For each index $i$, $\prob{\text{Bob succeeds}|~\text{Alice succeeds}}\geq 1 - \delta -  2 \delta^{1/4} \geq 1 - {\varepsilon} $.
nodes.label: claim:relativeprob

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.5
nodes.statement_short: Bound Bob's acceptance on S_A(rho') using Claim 3.3, then transfer to S_A(rho) via Claim 3.4 and trace distance.

nodes.name: Bob's acceptance on S_A(rho')
nodes.statement:
& \norm{(I_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S_A(\rho')} }^2 \geq \sum_{i,j=1}^N \abs{\braket{b_i}{g_j}}^2 \min\{g_j, \frac{1}{\delta}2^{c'}b_i \} \nonumber \\
& \geq \sum_{j=1}^N g_j \left(\sum_{i|~b_i\geq \delta 2^{-c'}g_j} \abs{\braket{b_i}{g_j}}^2 \right) \geq \sum_{j=1}^N g_j(1- \delta) = 1- \delta  . \quad \mbox{(using Claim~\ref{claim:1})}
nodes.label: eq:probonrho'

nodes.name: Bob's output is close to rho
nodes.statement: Given that both Alice and Bob succeed, fidelity between $\rho$ and the state of the register $B$ is at least $\sqrt{1 - \delta -  2 \delta^{1/4}} \geq 1 - {\varepsilon} $ .
assumptions: Given that both Alice and Bob succeed
conclusions: fidelity between $\rho$ and the state of the register $B$ is at least $\sqrt{1 - \delta -  2 \delta^{1/4}} \geq 1 - {\varepsilon} $
nodes.label: claim:boboutput

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.6
nodes.statement:
From gentle measurement lemma (Fact~\ref{fact:gentlemeasurement}), 
$$\mathrm{F}(S_A(\rho), \frac{(I_A\otimes P_B)\ketbra{S_A(\rho)} (I_A\otimes P_B) }{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } (I_A\otimes P_B)\ketbra{S_A(\rho)}}) \geq \sqrt{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } (I_A\otimes P_B)\ketbra{S_A(\rho)}}. $$ 
Since the marginal of $\ket{S_A(\rho)}$ on  register $B$ is $\rho$ and partial trace does not decrease fidelity (Fact~\ref{fact:monotonequantumoperation}), using item 2. above, the desired result follows.
nodes.statement_short: Gentle measurement lemma plus monotonicity of fidelity under partial trace.

nodes.name: Index agreement with high probability
nodes.statement: With probability at least $1-4{\varepsilon}$, $m=n=j$.
nodes.label: claim:highprobindex

nodes.name: Bad events T1, T2, T3
nodes.statement_short: T1: Alice never succeeds; T2: Alice's index m is not among Bob's successes; T3: Bob's chosen n differs from m.
nodes.label: def:badevent

nodes.name: Bounds on bad events
nodes.statement: It holds that: \quad $1. ~ \prob{T_1}\leq {\varepsilon}; \quad 2. ~ \prob{T_2}\leq{\varepsilon}; \quad 3. ~ \prob{T_3}\leq3{\varepsilon}.$
nodes.label: claim:protocol

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.9
nodes.statement_short: Bound each bad event: geometric tail for T1, Claim 3.5 for T2, Markov on |S_B| plus hash collision bound for T3.

nodes.name: Markov bound on |S_B|
nodes.statement: \prob{\abs{S_B} \geq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta{\varepsilon}}}\leq \frac{\delta{\varepsilon}}{2^{c'}} \cdot \expec{}{\abs{S_B}} \leq {\varepsilon} .
nodes.label: eq:sb

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.7
nodes.statement:
oindent{\em Proof of Claimef{claim:highprobindex}}.\quad We conclude the claim since,
$$\prob{n 
eq m} \leq\prob{T_1}+\prob{
eg T_1}\cdot\prob{T_3}\leq 4{\varepsilon}.$$ \qed
nodes.statement_short: Union bound over T1 and T3 using Claim 3.9.

nodes.name: Protocol with an upper bound on relative entropy
nodes.statement: Note that if Alice and Bob get a real number $r> \relent{\rho}{\sigma}$, instead of $\relent{\rho}{\sigma}$ (all other inputs remaining the same), the protocol above works in the same fashion, with the communication upper bounded by $O((r+1)/{\varepsilon}^4)$.
nodes.statement_short: The protocol works with any known upper bound r on S(rho||sigma), with O((r+1)/eps^4) communication.
nodes.label: qbevremark

nodes.name: Compression with side information (bipartite)
nodes.statement: Let $A,B$ be two registers. Alice is given the eigen-decomposition of a bipartite state $\rho_{AB} \in \mathcal{D}(AB)$. Bob is given the eigen-decompositions of a bipartite state $\sigma_{AB}\in \mathcal{D}(AB)$ and the state $\rho_A\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }_{B}(\rho_{AB})$, such that $\text{supp}(\rho_{AB})\subset \text{supp}(\sigma_{AB})$. Define $\sigma_A\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }_{B}(\sigma_{AB})$. Let  $\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}-\relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A}$ and ${\varepsilon} >0$ be known to Alice and Bob. There exists a protocol, in which Alice and Bob use shared entanglement and Alice sends $\CMcal{O}((\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}-\relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A}+1)/{\varepsilon}^4)$ bits of communication to Bob such that the state $\tilde{\rho}_{AB}$ that Bob outputs at the end of the protocol satisfies  $\mathrm{F}(\rho_{AB},\tilde{\rho}_{AB})\geq 1-5{\varepsilon}$ .
assumptions: Alice is given the eigen-decomposition of a bipartite state $\rho_{AB} \in \mathcal{D}(AB)$.
Let  $\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}-\relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A}$ and ${\varepsilon} >0$ be known to Alice and Bob.
conclusions: There exists a protocol, in which Alice and Bob use shared entanglement and Alice sends $\CMcal{O}((\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}-\relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A}+1)/{\varepsilon}^4)$ bits of communication to Bob
nodes.statement_short: If Bob also knows rho_A, communication drops to O((S(rho_AB||sigma_AB)-S(rho_A||sigma_A)+1)/eps^4).
nodes.label: lem:withsideinf

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.11
nodes.statement:
Following equality follows from definitions. 
\begin{equation*}
\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}-\relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A} = \relent{\rho_{AB}}{e^{\text{log}(\sigma_{AB})-\text{log}(\sigma_{A}\otimes I_B)+\text{log}(\rho_{A}\otimes I_B)}}  \enspace .
\end{equation*}
Define, 
$$Z= \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(e^{\text{log}(\sigma_{AB})-\text{log}(\sigma_{A}\otimes I_B)+\text{log}(\rho_{A}\otimes I_B)}) \quad ; \quad \tau_{AB}=e^{\text{log}(\sigma_{AB})-\text{log}(\sigma_{A}\otimes I_B)+\text{log}(\rho_{A}\otimes I_B)}/Z \enspace .$$ 
It holds that $Z\leq 1$ (from Fact \ref{fact:ruskai}) and hence $\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\tau_{AB}} \leq \relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}- \relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A}$. 
Bob computes the eigen-decomposition of $\tau_{AB}$ using his input. They run the protocol given by Theorem~\ref{thm:protocol} with the following setting: Alice knows a state $\rho_{AB}$, Bob knows a state $\tau_{AB}$ and both know a number
($=\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}- \relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A}$) greater than $\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\tau_{AB}}$.
 They also know the error parameter ${\varepsilon}>0$. By the virtue of Remark \ref{qbevremark}, at the end of the protocol, Bob obtains a state $\tilde{\rho}_{AB}$, such that $\mathrm{F}(\rho_{AB},\tilde{\rho}_{AB})\geq 1-5{\varepsilon}$. Communication from Alice is upper bounded by $\CMcal{O}(\br{\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}-\relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A} +1}/\epsilon^4)$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to Theorem 3.1 with Bob holding the normalized operator tau_AB, whose relative entropy from rho_AB is bounded via Fact 2.10.

nodes.name: Compression with channel side information (protocol P')
nodes.statement: Let $A,B$ be two registers associated to Hilbert spaces $\CMcal{H}_A,\CMcal{H}_B$ respectively. Alice and Bob know a Stinespring representation (Fact \ref{stinespring}) of a quantum channel $\mathcal{E}: \mathcal{L}(A)\rightarrow \mathcal{L}(B)$. Alice is given the eigen-decomposition of a state $\rho \in \mathcal{D}(A)$. Bob is given the eigen-decompositions of a state $\sigma \in \mathcal{D}(A)$ (such that $\text{supp}(\rho)\subset \text{supp}(\sigma)$) and the state $\rho'= \mathcal{E}(\rho)$. Let  $\relent{\rho}{\sigma}-\relent{\mathcal{E}(\rho)}{\mathcal{E}(\sigma)}$ and ${\varepsilon} >0$ be known to Alice and Bob. There exists a protocol, in which Alice and Bob use shared entanglement and Alice sends $\CMcal{O}((\relent{\rho}{\sigma}-\relent{\mathcal{E}(\rho)}{\mathcal{E}(\sigma)}+1)/{\varepsilon}^4)$ bits of communication to Bob, such that the state $\tilde{\rho}$ that Bob outputs at the end of the protocol satisfies  $\mathrm{F}(\rho,\tilde{\rho})\geq 1-5{\varepsilon}$ .
assumptions: Alice and Bob know a Stinespring representation (Fact \ref{stinespring}) of a quantum channel $\mathcal{E}: \mathcal{L}(A)\rightarrow \mathcal{L}(B)$.
Let  $\relent{\rho}{\sigma}-\relent{\mathcal{E}(\rho)}{\mathcal{E}(\sigma)}$ and ${\varepsilon} >0$ be known to Alice and Bob.
conclusions: There exists a protocol, in which Alice and Bob use shared entanglement and Alice sends $\CMcal{O}((\relent{\rho}{\sigma}-\relent{\mathcal{E}(\rho)}{\mathcal{E}(\sigma)}+1)/{\varepsilon}^4)$ bits of communication to Bob
nodes.statement_short: If Bob knows E(rho), communication is O((S(rho||sigma)-S(E(rho)||E(sigma))+1)/eps^4).
nodes.label: thm:sideinfchannel

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.12
nodes.statement:
Let a Stinespring representation of $\mathcal{E}$ be 
$\mathcal{E}(\omega) = 
\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }_{A,C}\br{V (\omega \ketbra{0}_{BC})V^{\dagger}}$, where  $V:\CMcal{H}_A \otimes \CMcal{H}_B \otimes \CMcal{H}_C \rightarrow \CMcal{H}_A \otimes \CMcal{H}_B\otimes \CMcal{H}_C$ is a unitary operation (Fact~\ref{stinespring}). Alice and Bob compute the states $V\br{\rho\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger}$ and $V\br{\sigma\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger}$ , respectively. From Lemma~\ref{lem:withsideinf} and the equality $\relent{V\br{\rho\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}}V^{\dagger}}{V\br{\sigma\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger}}=\relent{\rho}{\sigma}$, there exists a protocol, in which Alice and Bob use shared entanglement and Alice sends $\CMcal{O}(\relent{\rho}{\sigma}-\relent{\mathcal{E}(\rho)}{\mathcal{E}(\sigma)}+1)/{\varepsilon}^4 $ bits of communication to Bob, such that the state $\tilde{\rho}_{ABC}$ that Bob gets at the end of the protocol satisfies  $\mathrm{F}(V\br{\rho\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger},\tilde{\rho}_{ABC})\geq1-5{\varepsilon}$.  Bob outputs $\tilde{\rho} = \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }_{BC} V^{\dagger}\br{\tilde{\rho}_{ABC}} V $. From monotonicity of fidelity under quantum operation (Fact~\ref{fact:monotonequantumoperation}), $\mathrm{F}(\rho,  \tilde{\rho} )\geq1-5{\varepsilon}$.
nodes.statement_short: Dilate the channel via Stinespring and apply Lemma 3.11, then undo the isometry using monotonicity of fidelity.

nodes.name: Direct sum theorem for entanglement-assisted quantum one-way communication
nodes.statement:
Let $\CMcal{X},\CMcal{Y},\CMcal{Z}$ be finite sets, $f\subseteq\CMcal{X}\times\CMcal{Y}\times\CMcal{Z}$ be a relation, $0<{\varepsilon},\delta$ be error parameters and $k>1$ be an integer. We have
\[\dqcc{}{{\varepsilon}}{f^k}\geq \Omega \br{k \br{\delta^9\cdot\dqcc{}{{\varepsilon}+\delta}{f}-1}}.\]
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
assumptions: Let $\CMcal{X},\CMcal{Y},\CMcal{Z}$ be finite sets, $f\subseteq\CMcal{X}\times\CMcal{Y}\times\CMcal{Z}$ be a relation, $0<{\varepsilon},\delta$ be error parameters and $k>1$ be an integer.
nodes.statement_short: Computing k copies of f with error eps needs Omega(k(delta^9 Q_{eps+delta}(f) - 1)) communication.
nodes.label: thm:directsumoneway

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.1
nodes.statement:
Let  $\mu$ be any distribution over $\CMcal{X}\times\CMcal{Y}$. We show the following, which combined with Fact~\ref{fact:yaos principle} implies the desired:
\[\dqcc{, \mu^k}{{\varepsilon}}{f^k}\geq\Omega \br{k \br{\delta^9\cdot\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}+\delta}{f}-1}}.\]

Let $\CMcal{Q}$ be a quantum one-way protocol with communication $c\cdot k$ computing $f^k$  with  overall probability of success at least $1-{\varepsilon}$ under distribution $\mu^k$. Let the inputs to Alice and Bob be given in registers $X_1,X_2\ldots X_k$ and $Y_1,Y_2\ldots Y_k$. For brevity, we define $X\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } X_1,X_2\ldots X_k$ and $Y\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } Y_1,Y_2\ldots Y_k$. Thus, the state $\sum_{xy}\mu^k(x,y)\ketbra{xy}_{XY}$ represents the joint input, where $x$ is drawn from $X$ and $y$ is drawn from $Y$.

Let $\sigma_{E_A,E_B}$ be the shared entanglement between Alice and Bob where register $E_A$ is with Alice and $E_B$ with Bob. Alice applies unitary $U:\CMcal{H}_X\otimes \CMcal{H}_{E_A}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_X\otimes \CMcal{H}_A\otimes \CMcal{H}_M$, where $E_A\equiv AM$, sends the message register $M$ to Bob, and then Bob applies the unitary $V: \CMcal{H}_Y\otimes\CMcal{H}_M\otimes \CMcal{H}_{E_B}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_Y\otimes\CMcal{H}_{B'}\otimes\CMcal{H}_Z$, where $ME_B\equiv B'Z$. Since unitary operations by Alice and Bob are conditioned on their respective inputs, the unitaries $U,V$ are  of the form $U=\sum_x\ketbra{x}_X\otimes U_x$ and $V=\sum_y\ketbra{y}_Y\otimes V_y$, where $U_x:\CMcal{H}_{E_A}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_A\otimes \CMcal{H}_M$ and $V_y: \CMcal{H}_M\otimes \CMcal{H}_{E_B}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_{B'}\otimes\CMcal{H}_Z$.
Let the following be the global state before Alice applies her unitary:
$$\theta_{XYE_AE_B} = \sum_{xy}\mu^k(x,y)\ketbra{xy}_{XY}\otimes\sigma_{E_AE_B}.$$ 

Let $D=D_1\cdots D_k$ be a random variable uniformly distributed over $\set{0,1}^k$ and independent of the input $XY$. Define random variables $U_1,U_2\ldots U_k$ such that $U_i=X_i$ if $D_i=0$ and $U_i=Y_i$ if $D_i=1$. Let $U=U_1,U_2\ldots U_k$. Consider the state $\theta_{XYE_AE_BDU}$, with registers $D,U$ as defined above.

 Let $\rho_{XYAME_BDU}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } U\theta_{XYE_AE_BDU} U^{\dagger}$ be the state after Alice applies her unitary and sends $M$ to Bob. Since $$\condmutinf{XE_AE_B}{Y}{DU}_{\theta}=0,$$ it holds that  
\[\condmutinf{XAE_BM}{Y}{DU}_{\rho}=0.\]
From the definition of $DU$, we thus have (below $-i$ represents the set $\{1,2\ldots i-1,i+1\ldots k\}$),
\begin{equation} \condmutinf{X_{-i}AE_BM}{Y}{X_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}=\condmutinf{XAE_BM}{Y_{-i}}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}=0.
\end{equation}
Since $\log\abs{M}\leq ck$ and register $E_B$ is independent of registers $XYDU$ in the state $\rho_{E_BXYDU}$, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
\mutinf{XYDU}{ME_B}_{\rho}&=&\mutinf{XYDU}{E_B}_{\rho}+\condmutinf{XYDU}{M}{E_B}_{\rho}\\ &=& \condmutinf{XYDU}{M}{E_B}_{\rho} \leq 2 \log\abs{M} \leq 2ck,
\end{eqnarray*}
where the second last inequality is from Fact~\ref{fact:conditionalmutinf}.
Consider
\begin{eqnarray*}
2ck&\geq& \mutinf{XYDU}{ME_B}_{\rho}\geq \condmutinf{XY}{ME_B}{DU}_{\rho}\\ &\geq&\sum_{i=1}^k\condmutinf{X_iY_i}{ME_B}{DU}_{\rho} \quad (\text{Fact} ~\ref{fact:chainrulemutualinf})\\
&=& \sum_{i=1}^k \condmutinf{X_iY_i}{ME_B}{D_iU_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho} 	\\ &=&\frac{1}{2}\br{\sum_{i=1}^k\br{\condmutinf{X_i}{ME_B}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}+\condmutinf{Y_i}{ME_B}{X_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}}}\\
&\geq&\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^k\condmutinf{X_i}{ME_B}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}.
\end{eqnarray*}
where the last equality is from the definition of $DU$ and the last inequality is from Fact~\ref{fact:strongsubadditivity}.



Hence there exists $j\in[k]$ such that
\begin{equation} \condmutinf{X_j}{ME_B}{Y_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\rho}\leq 4c.
\end{equation}
Furthermore, we have 
\begin{equation} \mutinf{X_jY_j}{D_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\rho}= \mutinf{X_jY_j}{D_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\theta} = 0.
\end{equation}
since the unitary by Alice does not change the state on registers $DUXY$.

For brevity, set $B\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } ME_B$. Define the following states, which are obtained by conditioning on various classical registers: $$\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{\bra{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{BXYDU}\ket{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\bra{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{XYDU}\ket{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}},$$

$$\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{\bra{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{BXDU}\ket{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\bra{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{XDU}\ket{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}$$

$$\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{\bra{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{BYDU}\ket{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\bra{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{YDU}\ket{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}$$

From~(\ref{eqn:dumarkov}), we have
\[\condmutinf{Y}{B}{X_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\rho}=0.\]
which is equivalent to, using Fact \ref{fact:cqcondmut} and the fact that registers $X,Y,U,D$ are classical in $\rho_B$: 
$$\expec{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}\leftarrow X_jY_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}{\relent{\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}}=0.$$ This implies $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}=\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ for all $x_j,y_j,d_{-j}u_{-j}$. 

From~(\ref{eqn:directsummessagelength}), and Fact \ref{fact:cqcondmut},
$$\expec{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}\leftarrow X_jY_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}{\relent{\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}}\leq 4c.$$ 

Let 
$$G\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\set{(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j}):\relent{\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}\leq \frac{4c}{\delta}}.$$ By Markov's inequality, 
$$\prob{X_jY_jD_{-j}U_{-j}\in G}\geq1-\delta. $$

Now, we exhibit an entanglement-assisted one-way protocol $\CMcal{Q}'$ for $f$ with communication less than $c$ and distributional error ${\varepsilon}$ under distribution $\mu$. 
\begin{mdframed}
\bigskip
\begin{enumerate}
\item Alice and Bob share public coins according to distribution $\rho_{D_{-j}U_{-j}}$, and the shared entanglement needed to run the protocol $\CMcal{P}$ from Theorem ~\ref{thm:protocol}.
\item Alice and Bob are given the input  $(x,y)\sim\mu$. They embed the input to the $j$-th coordinate $X_jY_j$. The input is independent of shared randomness, from equation (\ref{eqn:directsumpubliccoins}). 
\item Given input $(x_j,y_j)\equiv (x,y)$ and shared public coins $d_{-j}u_{-j}$, Alice knows the eigen-decomposition of the state $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, since $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}=\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$. Bob knows the eigen-decomposition of state $\rho_{B}^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$.
\item They  run the protocol in Theorem ~\ref{thm:protocol} with inputs $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, $\frac{4c}{\delta}$ (given to Alice) and $\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, $\frac{4c}{\delta}$ (given to Bob). After communicating $\mathcal{O}(4c/\delta^9)$  bits to Bob, Bob receives a state $\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ satisfying $\|\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}-\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\|_1\leq \delta$ if $(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j})\in G$. 
\item Bob samples the distribution from $\rho_{Y_{-j}}$, since he has the registers $D_{-j}U_{-j}Y_j$. This is possible from equation \ref{eqn:dumarkov}, which states that register $Y_{-j}$ is independent of registers $A,B,X$ conditioned on registers $D_{-j}U_{-j}Y_j$. 
\item Bob applies the unitary $V$, as in the protocol $\CMcal{Q}$, on registers $BY\equiv E_BMY$ and then measures the register $Z$. He outputs the outcome. 
\end{enumerate}
\end{mdframed}
\bigskip
From the protocol, it is clear that overall distributional error in $\CMcal{Q}'$ is at most $2\delta+{\varepsilon}$. The error $2\delta$ occurs since the state $\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ satisfies $\|\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}-\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\|_1\leq \delta$ and the probability that $(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j})\notin G$ is at most $\delta$. The error ${\varepsilon}$ is due to the original protocol $\CMcal{Q}$.
Hence 
\[\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}+2\delta}{f}\leq \CMcal{O}((c+1)/\delta^9),\]
which implies (changing $\delta\rightarrow \frac{\delta}{2}$)
\[\dqcc{, \mu^k}{{\varepsilon}}{f^k}\geq\Omega \br{k \br{\delta^9\cdot\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}+\delta}{f}-1}}.\]

assumptions: Let $\rho,\sigma$ be quantum states on a Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}$ of dimension $N$.
Alice is given the eigen-decomposition of $\rho$ and Bob is given the eigen-decomposition of $\sigma$.
conclusions: There exists a zero-communication  protocol satisfying the following.
nodes.statement_short: Without communication, Alice and Bob can produce registers with marginals rho, sigma such that a common projective measurement agrees w.p. >= (1-sqrt(||rho-sigma||_1 - ||rho-sigma||_1^2/4))^3.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.1
nodes.statement_short: Construction: both parties run quantum rejection sampling on shared maximally entangled copies; the output state overlaps a symmetric state theta on which any common measurement agrees.

nodes.name: Marginals of the output
nodes.statement: $\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }_{A_2B_1B_2}(\tau)=\rho$ and $\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }_{A_1A_2B_2}(\tau)=\sigma$.
nodes.label: redstate

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 5.2
nodes.statement: It is easily seen that the marginal of the state $(P_A \otimes I_B) \ket{S}$ in register $A$  is $\rho$. Similarly the marginal of the state $(I_A \otimes P_B) \ket{S}$ in register $B$ in  is $\sigma$.
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation of marginals of the projected shared state.

nodes.name: Lower bound on output state tau
nodes.statement_short: tau dominates the normalized state from both succeeding at the same index.
nodes.label: claim:tau

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 5.3
nodes.statement:
Consider the event that Alice and Bob succeed at the same index. The resulting state in $AA_1BB_1$ is 
$$\frac{(P_A\otimes P_B ) \ket{S}\bra{S} (P_A\otimes P_B)}{\bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}},$$ 
and this event occurs with probability 
$$\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\bra{S}(I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}^{i} \cdot \bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}= \frac{\bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}}{1 - \bra{S}(I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}}.$$ 
Since the cases of Bob succeeding before Alice and Alice succeeding before Bob add positive operators to $\tau$, we get the desired.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the geometric series for the event that both succeed at the same index; other cases add positive operators.

nodes.name: Overlap of tau with theta
nodes.statement:
Let $\ket{\theta} \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{(P_A\otimes P_A)\ket{S}}{\norm{(P_A\otimes P_A)\ket{S}}}$. Then 
$$\bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta} \geq \frac{\left(1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2}\right)^2}{1 + \sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2}} \geq \left(1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2}\right)^3 .$$
nodes.statement_short: <theta|tau|theta> >= (1 - sqrt(||rho-sigma||_1 - ||rho-sigma||_1^2/4))^3.
nodes.label: overlaptau

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 5.4
nodes.statement:
Consider,
\begin{align*}
\bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta} &\geq   \frac{ \abs{\bra{\theta}P_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}}^2}{1 - \bra{S} (I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}} &  \mbox{(Claim~\ref{claim:tau})}\\ 
& = \frac{ \abs{\bra{\theta}P_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}}^2}{2/N-\bra{S}P_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}} & \mbox{(using $\bra{S}P_A\otimes I_B\ket{S}=\bra{S}I_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}=1/N$)}.
\end{align*}

By direct calculation, we get 
$$(P_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{KN}}\sum_{i,j}\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\braket{b_j}{a_i}\ket{b_j}\sum_{m=1}^{K\min(a_i,b_j)}\ket{m,m} ;$$ 
$$\ket{\theta}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{K}}\sum_i\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\ket{a_i}\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m,m} .$$ 
Hence,
\begin{equation} \bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta} \geq \frac{\left(\sum_{i,j}\min(a_i,b_j) \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2\right)^2}{2-\sum_{i,j}\min(a_i,b_j) \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2} .
\end{equation}

Define $R_{ij}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } a_i \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2$ and $R'_{ij}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } b_i \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2$. Note that both $\{R_{ij}\}$ and $\{R'_{ij}\}$ form probability distributions over $[N^2]$. Also note that $\mathrm{F}(R,R') = \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma})$. Consider (using relation between fidelity and $\ell_1$ distance, Facts~\ref{fact:fidelityvstrace} and~\ref{fact:tracefidelityequi}),
\begin{align}
 \sum_{i,j}\min(R_{ij},R'_{i,j}) & = 1 - \frac{1}{2}\onenorm{R-R'}  \geq 1 - \sqrt{1-\mathrm{F}(R,R')^2} \nonumber \\
 &= 1 - \sqrt{1-(\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } \sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma})^2}  \geq  1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2} . 
  \end{align}
  Combining Equations~\eqref{eq:thetatau} and~\eqref{eq:minR} we get the desired.
nodes.statement_short: Use Claim 5.3, compute the overlap explicitly as sum of minima of two distributions, and bound via fidelity/trace-distance relations.

\sum_{i,j}\min(R_{ij},R'_{i,j}) & = 1 - \frac{1}{2}\onenorm{R-R'}  \geq 1 - \sqrt{1-\mathrm{F}(R,R')^2} \nonumber \\

nodes.name: Protocol P (quantum compression)
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Input:} Alice is given $\rho=\sum_{i=1}^Na_i\ketbra{a_i}$. Bob is given $\sigma=\sum_{i=1}^Nb_i\ketbra{b_i}$.
\bigskip



\textbf{Shared resources:} Alice and Bob hold $\lceil N\log(\frac{1}{\delta}) \rceil$ registers $A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i$ ($i \in [\lceil N\log(\frac{1}{\delta}) \rceil]$), such that $A_1^i\equiv A_1, A^i_2\equiv A_2, B_1^i\equiv B_1,B_2^i\equiv B_2$. The shared state in register $A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i$ is $\ket{S}_{A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i}$. Let $i$ refer to the `index' of corresponding registers.

They also share infinitely many random hash functions $h_1,h_2,\cdots$, where each $h_l:\set{0,\cdots,N-1}\rightarrow\set{0,1}$.

\begin{enumerate}

\item \textbf{For} $i=1$ to $\lceil N\log(\frac{1}{\delta}) \rceil$,

\begin{enumerate}

\item Alice performs the measurement $\set{P_A,I_A- P_A}$ on each register $A_1^iA^i_2$ where,
\begin{equation} P_A\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\sum_i\ket{a_i}_{A_1}\bra{a_i}_{A_1}\otimes\left(\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m}_{A_2}\bra{m}_{A_2}\right) .
\end{equation}

On each index $i$, she declares \textit{success} if her outcome corresponds to $P_A$.

\item Bob performs the measurement $\set{P_B,I_B- P_B}$ on each register $B_1^iB^i_2$ where,
\begin{equation} P_B\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \sum_i\ket{b_i}_{B_1}\bra{b_i}_{B_1}\otimes\left(\sum_{m=1}^{\min\{\frac{K}{\delta} 2^{c'} b_i,K\}}\ket{m}_{B_2}\bra{m}_{B_2}\right) .
\end{equation}

On each index $i$, he declares \textit{success} if his outcome corresponds to $P_B$.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{Endfor}

\item If Alice does not succeed on any index, she aborts.

\item Else, Alice selects the first index $m$ where she succeeds and sends to Bob the binary encoding of $k=\lceil m/N\rceil$ using $\lceil\log\log\frac{1}{\delta}\rceil$ bits.  

\item Alice sends $\{ h_l(m\mod N) |~ l \in  [\lceil r + 2\log\frac{1}{\delta}\rceil]\}$  to Bob.

\item  Define $S_B \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \{ t |~ \text{ Bob succeeds on index } $t$\} \cap \{(k-1)N,  \cdots, k N -1\}$. If $S_B$ is empty, he outputs $\ketbra{0}$. Bob selects the first index $n$ in $S_B$ such that $\forall l \in  [\lceil r + 2\log\frac{1}{\delta}\rceil]: h_l(n \mod N) = h_l(m \mod N) $ and outputs the state in $B_1^n$ (if no such index exists, he outputs $\ketbra{0}$).

After communicating $\mathcal{O}(4c/\delta^9)$  bits to Bob, Bob receives a state $\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ satisfying $\|\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}-\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\|_1\leq \delta$ if $(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j})\in G$. 
\item Bob samples the distribution from $\rho_{Y_{-j}}$, since he has the registers $D_{-j}U_{-j}Y_j$. This is possible from equation \ref{eqn:dumarkov}, which states that register $Y_{-j}$ is independent of registers $A,B,X$ conditioned on registers $D_{-j}U_{-j}Y_j$. 
\item Bob applies the unitary $V$, as in the protocol $\CMcal{Q}$, on registers $BY\equiv E_BMY$ and then measures the register $Z$. He outputs the outcome.

nodes.name: Run protocol P
nodes.statement: They  run the protocol in Theorem ~\ref{thm:protocol} with inputs $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, $\frac{4c}{\delta}$ (given to Alice) and $\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$, $\frac{4c}{\delta}$ (given to Bob). After communicating $\mathcal{O}(4c/\delta^9)$  bits to Bob, Bob receives a state $\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ satisfying $\|\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}-\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\|_1\leq \delta$ if $(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j})\in G$.
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Run protocol P with relative entropy bound 4c/delta.

nodes.name: Sample remaining inputs
nodes.statement: Bob samples the distribution from $\rho_{Y_{-j}}$, since he has the registers $D_{-j}U_{-j}Y_j$.
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Bob samples Y_{-j} conditioned on his registers.

nodes.name: Finish Q and output
nodes.statement: Bob applies the unitary $V$, as in the protocol $\CMcal{Q}$, on registers $BY\equiv E_BMY$ and then measures the register $Z$. He outputs the outcome.
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Bob applies V, measures Z and outputs.

nodes.name: Quantum correlated sampling protocol
output: Let $A \equiv A_1A_2$ and $B\equiv B_1B_2$ be used as output registers.
nodes.statement_short: Each party independently performs rejection-sampling measurements on shared entangled copies and keeps its first success, with no communication.

nodes.name: Shared resources
nodes.statement: \textbf{Shared resources:} Alice and Bob hold infinitely many registers $A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i$ ($i>0$), such that $A_1^i\equiv A_1, A^i_2\equiv A_2, B_1^i\equiv B_1,B_2^i\equiv B_2$. The shared state in register $A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i$ is $\ket{S}_{A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i}$. Let $A \equiv A_1A_2$ and $B\equiv B_1B_2$ be used as output registers. Let $i$ refer to the `index' of corresponding registers.
nodes.statement_short: Shared resources.

nodes.name: Alice samples
nodes.statement_short: Alice measures copies until first success and keeps that register.

nodes.name: Bob samples
nodes.statement_short: Bob measures copies until first success and keeps that register.

nodes.name: Purify
nodes.statement: Introduce a register $B$, such that $|B|\geq |A|$. Let $\phi\in \mathcal{D}(AB)$ be a purification of $\rho$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce a purification phi of rho.

nodes.name: Projected purification
nodes.statement: Then $( \Pi \otimes I_B)\phi ( \Pi \otimes I_B)$ is a purification of $\Pi \rho \Pi $.
nodes.statement_short: The projected phi purifies the projected rho.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement:
Hence  (using monotonicity of fidelity under quantum operation, Fact~\ref{fact:monotonequantumoperation})
\[\mathrm{F}(\rho, \frac{\Pi \rho \Pi}{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } \Pi \rho } )\mathrm{F}\br{\phi,(\Pi\otimes I_B)\phi(\Pi\otimes I_B)}= \frac{\abs{\bra{\phi}(\Pi \otimes I) \ket{\phi}}}{\norm{(\Pi \otimes I) \ket{\phi}}}  = \sqrt{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }( \Pi \rho)}.   \tag*{\qedhere} \]
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of fidelity gives the bound.

nodes.name: Chain rule computation
nodes.statement_short: Split off A_1 by the chain rule and use independence.

nodes.name: Justify each step
nodes.statement: The first and second equalities follow from the definition of the conditional mutual information. The third equality is from the independence between $A_1$ and $A_2A_3\ldots A_k$. The last inequality is from strong subadditivity (Fact~\ref{fact:strongsubadditivity}).
nodes.statement_short: Justify via definitions, independence and strong subadditivity.

nodes.name: Induction
nodes.statement: Proof follows by induction.
nodes.statement_short: Iterate by induction.

nodes.name: Setup eigen-decompositions and parameters
nodes.statement: Let the eigen-decomposition of $\rho$ be $\sum_{i=1}^Na_i\ketbra{a_i}$ and that of $\sigma$ be $\sum_{i=1}^Nb_i\ketbra{b_i}$. Define $c\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\relent{\rho}{\sigma}$, $\delta \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } ({\varepsilon}/3)^4$ and $c' \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } (c+2)/\delta$. Without loss of generality, assume $a_1,a_2\ldots a_N, \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta}b_1,\frac{2^{c'}}{\delta}b_2\ldots \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta}b_N$ to be rational numbers, and define $K$ be the least common multiple of their denominators. The error due to this assumption can be made arbitrarily close to $0$, for large enough $K$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix eigen-decompositions, c, delta=(eps/3)^4, c'=(c+2)/delta and the rational approximation K.

nodes.name: Introduce registers
nodes.statement: Let $\set{\ket{1},\ket{2}\ldots \ket{N}}$ be an orthonormal basis for $\CMcal{H}$. Introduce registers $A_1,B_1$ associated to $\CMcal{H}$ and registers $A_2,B_2$ associated to some Hilbert space $\CMcal{H}'$ with an orthonormal basis $\set{\ket{1},\ket{2}\ldots \ket{K}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce registers.

nodes.name: Shared state
nodes.statement:
Consider the following state on $A_1,A_2,B_1,B_2$. 
\begin{equation} \ket{S}_{A_1A_2B_1B_2} \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{1}{\sqrt{KN}}\sum_{i=1}^N \ket{i,i}_{A_1B_1} \otimes \left( \sum_{m=1}^{K}\ket{m, m}_{A_2B_2} \right)
\end{equation}

For brevity, define registers $A,B$ such that $A\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } A_1A_2$ and $B\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } B_1B_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the shared maximally entangled state |S>.

nodes.name: The protocol
nodes.statement_short: Describe protocol P.

nodes.name: Success probabilities (Claim 3.2)
nodes.statement_short: Success probabilities (Claim 3.2).

nodes.name: Apply substate theorem
nodes.statement: From quantum substrate theorem (Fact \ref{fact:substrate}), there exists a state $\rho'$ which satisfies $\mathrm{F}(\rho,\rho')\geq 1-\delta$ and $$\rminent{\rho'}{\sigma}\leq\frac{\relent{\rho}{\sigma}+1}{\delta}+\log\frac{1}{1-\delta}\leq \frac{\relent{\rho}{\sigma}+2}{\delta}=c'.$$
nodes.statement_short: Obtain rho' close to rho with relative max-entropy at most c'.

nodes.name: Claim 3.3
nodes.statement_short: Claim 3.3.

nodes.name: Define S_A states
nodes.statement:
Define 
$$\ket{S_A(\rho)}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{1}{\sqrt{K}}\sum_{i=1}^N\ket{a_i}\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\otimes \left(\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m, m}\right) ; $$
$$\ket{S_A(\rho')}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\frac{1}{\sqrt{K}}\sum_{i=1}^N\ket{g_i}\ket{\conjugate{g_i}}\otimes \left(\sum_{m=1}^{\lceil Kg_i \rceil}\ket{m, m} \right) .$$
Here $\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}$ (similarly $\ket{\conjugate{g_i}}$) is the state obtained by taking complex conjugate of  $\ket{a_i}$ ($\ket{g_i}$), with respect to the basis $\set{\ket{1},\ket{2}\ldots \ket{N}}$ in $\CMcal{H}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the post-success states S_A(rho), S_A(rho').

nodes.name: Claim 3.4
nodes.statement_short: Claim 3.4.

nodes.name: Claim 3.5
nodes.statement_short: Claim 3.5.

nodes.name: Claim 3.6
nodes.statement_short: Claim 3.6.

nodes.name: Claim 3.7 statement
nodes.statement:
Let $j$ be the first index where Alice and Bob both succeed. As described in the protocol, $m$ is the first index where Alice succeeds and $n$ is the index such that Bob outputs the state in $B_1^n$. 
We have the following claim, 

\begin{claim} With probability at least $1-4{\varepsilon}$, $m=n=j$.
\end{claim}
nodes.statement_short: Claim 3.7 statement.

nodes.name: Bad events
nodes.statement_short: Bad events.

nodes.name: Claim 3.9
nodes.statement_short: Claim 3.9.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.7
nodes.statement:
We bound the probability that $m\neq n$. If $m=n$, then $m$ being the first index on which Alice succeeds, we have $m=n=j$. 

\bigskip

\noindent{\em Proof of Claim\ref{claim:highprobindex}}.\quad We conclude the claim since,
$$\prob{n \neq m} \leq\prob{T_1}+\prob{\neg T_1}\cdot\prob{T_3}\leq 4{\varepsilon}.$$ \qed
nodes.statement_short: Proof of Claim 3.7.

nodes.name: Fidelity of Bob's output
nodes.statement: From claims \ref{claim:successprob},\ref{claim:relativeprob} and \ref{claim:highprobindex}, the probability that Bob learns the index $j$ is atleast $1-4{\varepsilon}$. Conditioned on this event, Claim \ref{claim:boboutput}, implies that the state $\rho' \in \mathcal{D}(B^j)$ that Bob outputs satisfies $\mathrm{F}(\rho',\rho)\geq 1-{\varepsilon}$. Conditioned on the event that Bob learns the wrong index or the protocol is aborted, let the state output by Bob be $\mu$. Then Bob outputs the state $\tilde{\rho}=\alpha\rho'+(1-\alpha)\mu$, where $\alpha\geq 1-4{\varepsilon}$. Using concavity of fidelity (Fact \ref{fact:fidconcave}), we have $\mathrm{F}(\tilde{\rho},\rho)\geq \alpha\mathrm{F}(\rho',\rho)+(1-\alpha)\mathrm{F}(\mu,\rho) \geq (1-4{\varepsilon})(1-{\varepsilon})\geq 1- 5{\varepsilon}$.
nodes.statement_short: Mix good and bad outcomes and use joint concavity of fidelity to get 1-5eps.

nodes.name: Communication cost
nodes.statement: The communication cost of above protocol is $$\lceil\log\log\frac{1}{{\varepsilon}}\rceil+\lceil c' + \log\frac{1}{\delta} + 2\log\frac{1}{{\varepsilon}}\rceil\leq \lceil 3^4\frac{c+2}{{\varepsilon}^4}+7\log\frac{1}{{\varepsilon}} \rceil.$$ This completes the proof of theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Count bits sent.

nodes.name: Operator inequality
nodes.statement: Since  $\rho' \leq 2^{c'}\sigma$, it implies $g_i\ket{g_i}\bra{g_i} \leq 2^{c'}\sigma$.
nodes.statement_short: Operator inequality.

nodes.name: Projector onto small eigenspace
nodes.statement: Let $\Pi$ be the projection onto the eigen-space of $\sigma$ with eigenvalues less than or equal to $p\cdot g_i$. We have $\Pi\sigma\Pi \leq p\cdot g_i\cdot\Pi$.
nodes.statement_short: Projector onto small eigenspace.

nodes.name: Project and conclude
nodes.statement: After applying $\Pi$ on both sides of the equation $g_i\ket{g_i}\bra{g_i} \leq 2^{c'}\sigma$ and taking operator norm on both sides, we get $g_i\sum_{j:~b_j \leq p\cdot g_i}\abs{\braket{b_j}{g_i}}^2 \leq 2^{c'}\cdot p \cdot g_i $. This implies the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Project and conclude.

nodes.name: Define distributions R, R'
nodes.statement: Define $R_{ij}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } a_i \abs{\braket{a_i}{g_j}}^2$ and $R'_{ij}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } g_i \abs{\braket{a_i}{g_j}}^2$. Note that both $R \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \{R_{ij}\}$ and $R' \ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \{R'_{ij}\}$ form probability distributions over $[N^2]$. Also note that $\mathrm{F}(R,R') = \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\rho'})$.
nodes.statement_short: Define distributions R, R'.

nodes.name: Chain of inequalities
nodes.statement_short: Chain of inequalities.

nodes.name: Bound T1
nodes.statement: $\prob{T_1}\leq\br{1-\frac{1}{N}}^{\lceil N \cdot \log\frac{1}{{\varepsilon}}\rceil}\leq \exp^{-\lceil\log\frac{1}{{\varepsilon}}\rceil}\leq  \delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound T1.

nodes.name: Bound T2
nodes.statement: Follows from Claim \ref{claim:relativeprob}.
nodes.statement_short: Bound T2.

nodes.name: Bound T3
nodes.statement_short: Bound T3.

nodes.name: Expected size of S_B
nodes.statement: For this argument we condition on $\neg T_1$ for all events below. From Claim \ref{claim:successprob} and the fact that Bob independently measures each index, we have  $\expec{}{\abs{S_B}}= N\cdot \prob{\text{Bob succeeds}} \leq \frac{2^{c'}}{\delta}$.
nodes.statement_short: Expected size of S_B.

nodes.name: Markov
nodes.statement_short: Markov.

nodes.name: Union and hash collision bound
nodes.statement_short: Union and hash collision bound.

nodes.name: Rewrite difference of relative entropies
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite difference of relative entropies.

nodes.name: Normalize tau
nodes.statement:
Define, 
$$Z= \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(e^{\text{log}(\sigma_{AB})-\text{log}(\sigma_{A}\otimes I_B)+\text{log}(\rho_{A}\otimes I_B)}) \quad ; \quad \tau_{AB}=e^{\text{log}(\sigma_{AB})-\text{log}(\sigma_{A}\otimes I_B)+\text{log}(\rho_{A}\otimes I_B)}/Z \enspace .$$ 
It holds that $Z\leq 1$ (from Fact \ref{fact:ruskai}) and hence $\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\tau_{AB}} \leq \relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}- \relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define tau=exp(...)/Z with Z<=1 by Fact 2.10.

nodes.name: Run protocol P
nodes.statement:
Bob computes the eigen-decomposition of $\tau_{AB}$ using his input. They run the protocol given by Theorem~\ref{thm:protocol} with the following setting: Alice knows a state $\rho_{AB}$, Bob knows a state $\tau_{AB}$ and both know a number
($=\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}- \relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A}$) greater than $\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\tau_{AB}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Run protocol P.

nodes.name: Conclude via Remark 3.10
nodes.statement: They also know the error parameter ${\varepsilon}>0$. By the virtue of Remark \ref{qbevremark}, at the end of the protocol, Bob obtains a state $\tilde{\rho}_{AB}$, such that $\mathrm{F}(\rho_{AB},\tilde{\rho}_{AB})\geq 1-5{\varepsilon}$. Communication from Alice is upper bounded by $\CMcal{O}(\br{\relent{\rho_{AB}}{\sigma_{AB}}-\relent{\rho_A}{\sigma_A} +1}/\epsilon^4)$.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude via Remark 3.10.

nodes.name: Stinespring dilation
nodes.statement:
Let a Stinespring representation of $\mathcal{E}$ be 
$\mathcal{E}(\omega) = 
\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }_{A,C}\br{V (\omega \ketbra{0}_{BC})V^{\dagger}}$, where  $V:\CMcal{H}_A \otimes \CMcal{H}_B \otimes \CMcal{H}_C \rightarrow \CMcal{H}_A \otimes \CMcal{H}_B\otimes \CMcal{H}_C$ is a unitary operation (Fact~\ref{stinespring}). Alice and Bob compute the states $V\br{\rho\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger}$ and $V\br{\sigma\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger}$ , respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Stinespring dilation.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 3.11
nodes.statement: From Lemma~\ref{lem:withsideinf} and the equality $\relent{V\br{\rho\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}}V^{\dagger}}{V\br{\sigma\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger}}=\relent{\rho}{\sigma}$, there exists a protocol, in which Alice and Bob use shared entanglement and Alice sends $\CMcal{O}(\relent{\rho}{\sigma}-\relent{\mathcal{E}(\rho)}{\mathcal{E}(\sigma)}+1)/{\varepsilon}^4 $ bits of communication to Bob, such that the state $\tilde{\rho}_{ABC}$ that Bob gets at the end of the protocol satisfies  $\mathrm{F}(V\br{\rho\otimes\ketbra{0}_{BC}} V^{\dagger},\tilde{\rho}_{ABC})\geq1-5{\varepsilon}$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 3.11.

nodes.name: Undo dilation
nodes.statement: Bob outputs $\tilde{\rho} = \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }_{BC} V^{\dagger}\br{\tilde{\rho}_{ABC}} V $. From monotonicity of fidelity under quantum operation (Fact~\ref{fact:monotonequantumoperation}), $\mathrm{F}(\rho,  \tilde{\rho} )\geq1-5{\varepsilon}$.
nodes.statement_short: Undo dilation.

nodes.name: Reduce to distributional statement
nodes.statement:
Let  $\mu$ be any distribution over $\CMcal{X}\times\CMcal{Y}$. We show the following, which combined with Fact~\ref{fact:yaos principle} implies the desired:
\[\dqcc{, \mu^k}{{\varepsilon}}{f^k}\geq\Omega \br{k \br{\delta^9\cdot\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}+\delta}{f}-1}}.\]
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to distributional statement.

nodes.name: k-fold protocol Q
nodes.statement: Let $\CMcal{Q}$ be a quantum one-way protocol with communication $c\cdot k$ computing $f^k$  with  overall probability of success at least $1-{\varepsilon}$ under distribution $\mu^k$. Let the inputs to Alice and Bob be given in registers $X_1,X_2\ldots X_k$ and $Y_1,Y_2\ldots Y_k$. For brevity, we define $X\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } X_1,X_2\ldots X_k$ and $Y\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } Y_1,Y_2\ldots Y_k$. Thus, the state $\sum_{xy}\mu^k(x,y)\ketbra{xy}_{XY}$ represents the joint input, where $x$ is drawn from $X$ and $y$ is drawn from $Y$.
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: k-fold protocol Q.

nodes.name: Unitaries and global state
nodes.statement:
Let $\sigma_{E_A,E_B}$ be the shared entanglement between Alice and Bob where register $E_A$ is with Alice and $E_B$ with Bob. Alice applies unitary $U:\CMcal{H}_X\otimes \CMcal{H}_{E_A}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_X\otimes \CMcal{H}_A\otimes \CMcal{H}_M$, where $E_A\equiv AM$, sends the message register $M$ to Bob, and then Bob applies the unitary $V: \CMcal{H}_Y\otimes\CMcal{H}_M\otimes \CMcal{H}_{E_B}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_Y\otimes\CMcal{H}_{B'}\otimes\CMcal{H}_Z$, where $ME_B\equiv B'Z$. Since unitary operations by Alice and Bob are conditioned on their respective inputs, the unitaries $U,V$ are  of the form $U=\sum_x\ketbra{x}_X\otimes U_x$ and $V=\sum_y\ketbra{y}_Y\otimes V_y$, where $U_x:\CMcal{H}_{E_A}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_A\otimes \CMcal{H}_M$ and $V_y: \CMcal{H}_M\otimes \CMcal{H}_{E_B}\rightarrow \CMcal{H}_{B'}\otimes\CMcal{H}_Z$.
Let the following be the global state before Alice applies her unitary:
$$\theta_{XYE_AE_B} = \sum_{xy}\mu^k(x,y)\ketbra{xy}_{XY}\otimes\sigma_{E_AE_B}.$$
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Unitaries and global state.

nodes.name: Registers D, U
nodes.statement: Let $D=D_1\cdots D_k$ be a random variable uniformly distributed over $\set{0,1}^k$ and independent of the input $XY$. Define random variables $U_1,U_2\ldots U_k$ such that $U_i=X_i$ if $D_i=0$ and $U_i=Y_i$ if $D_i=1$. Let $U=U_1,U_2\ldots U_k$. Consider the state $\theta_{XYE_AE_BDU}$, with registers $D,U$ as defined above.
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Registers D, U.

nodes.name: Markov conditions
nodes.statement:
Let $\rho_{XYAME_BDU}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } U\theta_{XYE_AE_BDU} U^{\dagger}$ be the state after Alice applies her unitary and sends $M$ to Bob. Since $$\condmutinf{XE_AE_B}{Y}{DU}_{\theta}=0,$$ it holds that  
\[\condmutinf{XAE_BM}{Y}{DU}_{\rho}=0.\]
From the definition of $DU$, we thus have (below $-i$ represents the set $\{1,2\ldots i-1,i+1\ldots k\}$),
\begin{equation} \condmutinf{X_{-i}AE_BM}{Y}{X_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}=\condmutinf{XAE_BM}{Y_{-i}}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}=0.
\end{equation}
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Derive conditional independence relations (6).

nodes.name: Bound total information
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Bound total information.

nodes.name: Split information over coordinates
nodes.statement:
Consider
\begin{eqnarray*}
2ck&\geq& \mutinf{XYDU}{ME_B}_{\rho}\geq \condmutinf{XY}{ME_B}{DU}_{\rho}\\ &\geq&\sum_{i=1}^k\condmutinf{X_iY_i}{ME_B}{DU}_{\rho} \quad (\text{Fact} ~\ref{fact:chainrulemutualinf})\\
&=& \sum_{i=1}^k \condmutinf{X_iY_i}{ME_B}{D_iU_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho} 	\\ &=&\frac{1}{2}\br{\sum_{i=1}^k\br{\condmutinf{X_i}{ME_B}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}+\condmutinf{Y_i}{ME_B}{X_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}}}\\
&\geq&\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^k\condmutinf{X_i}{ME_B}{Y_iD_{-i}U_{-i}}_{\rho}.
\end{eqnarray*}
where the last equality is from the definition of $DU$ and the last inequality is from Fact~\ref{fact:strongsubadditivity}.
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Split information over coordinates.

nodes.name: Choose coordinate j
nodes.statement:
Hence there exists $j\in[k]$ such that
\begin{equation} \condmutinf{X_j}{ME_B}{Y_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\rho}\leq 4c.
\end{equation}
Furthermore, we have 
\begin{equation} \mutinf{X_jY_j}{D_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\rho}= \mutinf{X_jY_j}{D_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\theta} = 0.
\end{equation}
since the unitary by Alice does not change the state on registers $DUXY$.
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Pick j with information at most 4c, independent of public coins.

nodes.name: Conditional states
nodes.statement:
For brevity, set $B\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } ME_B$. Define the following states, which are obtained by conditioning on various classical registers: $$\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{\bra{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{BXYDU}\ket{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\bra{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{XYDU}\ket{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}},$$

$$\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{\bra{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{BXDU}\ket{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\bra{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{XDU}\ket{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}$$

$$\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } \frac{\bra{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{BYDU}\ket{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\bra{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\rho_{YDU}\ket{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}$$
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Conditional states.

nodes.name: Alice's state independent of y_j
nodes.statement:
From~(\ref{eqn:dumarkov}), we have
\[\condmutinf{Y}{B}{X_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}_{\rho}=0.\]
which is equivalent to, using Fact \ref{fact:cqcondmut} and the fact that registers $X,Y,U,D$ are classical in $\rho_B$: 
$$\expec{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}\leftarrow X_jY_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}{\relent{\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}}=0.$$ This implies $\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}=\rho_B^{x_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ for all $x_j,y_j,d_{-j}u_{-j}$.
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Alice's state independent of y_j.

nodes.name: Expected relative entropy
nodes.statement:
From~(\ref{eqn:directsummessagelength}), and Fact \ref{fact:cqcondmut},
$$\expec{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}\leftarrow X_jY_jD_{-j}U_{-j}}{\relent{\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}}\leq 4c.$$
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Expected relative entropy.

nodes.name: Good set G
nodes.statement:
Let 
$$G\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} }\set{(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j}):\relent{\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}{\rho_B^{y_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}}\leq \frac{4c}{\delta}}.$$ By Markov's inequality, 
$$\prob{X_jY_jD_{-j}U_{-j}\in G}\geq1-\delta. $$
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Good set G.

nodes.name: Protocol Q'
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Protocol Q'.

nodes.name: Error analysis
nodes.statement: From the protocol, it is clear that overall distributional error in $\CMcal{Q}'$ is at most $2\delta+{\varepsilon}$. The error $2\delta$ occurs since the state $\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}$ satisfies $\|\sigma_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}-\rho_B^{x_jy_jd_{-j}u_{-j}}\|_1\leq \delta$ and the probability that $(x_j,y_j,d_{-j},u_{-j})\notin G$ is at most $\delta$. The error ${\varepsilon}$ is due to the original protocol $\CMcal{Q}$.
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Error analysis.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement:
Hence 
\[\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}+2\delta}{f}\leq \CMcal{O}((c+1)/\delta^9),\]
which implies (changing $\delta\rightarrow \frac{\delta}{2}$)
\[\dqcc{, \mu^k}{{\varepsilon}}{f^k}\geq\Omega \br{k \br{\delta^9\cdot\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}+\delta}{f}-1}}.\]
nodes.section: 4 A direct sum theorem for quantum one-way communication complexity
nodes.statement_short: Conclude.

nodes.name: Setup

nodes.statement:
Finally  using monotonicity of fidelity under quantum operation (Fact~\ref{fact:monotonequantumoperation}) and Claim~\ref{overlaptau} we get the second part of the theorem as follows. 
\[\sqrt{\ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} } (E\tau)} \geq  \mathrm{F}(\tau , \ketbra{\theta}) = \sqrt{\bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta}} \geq \left(1-\sqrt{\onenorm{\rho-\sigma} - \frac{1}{4}\onenorm{\rho-\sigma}^2}\right)^{3/2} . \tag*{\qedhere} \]

nodes.name: Same-index event
nodes.statement:
Consider the event that Alice and Bob succeed at the same index. The resulting state in $AA_1BB_1$ is 
$$\frac{(P_A\otimes P_B ) \ket{S}\bra{S} (P_A\otimes P_B)}{\bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}},$$ 
and this event occurs with probability 
$$\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\bra{S}(I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}^{i} \cdot \bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}= \frac{\bra{S}(P_A \otimes P_B)\ket{S}}{1 - \bra{S}(I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Same-index event.

nodes.statement:
By direct calculation, we get 
$$(P_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{KN}}\sum_{i,j}\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\braket{b_j}{a_i}\ket{b_j}\sum_{m=1}^{K\min(a_i,b_j)}\ket{m,m} ;$$ 
$$\ket{\theta}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{K}}\sum_i\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\ket{a_i}\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m,m} .$$ 
Hence,
\begin{equation} \bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta} \geq \frac{\left(\sum_{i,j}\min(a_i,b_j) \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2\right)^2}{2-\sum_{i,j}\min(a_i,b_j) \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2} .
\end{equation}
